note: 氣死了 qì sǐ le 'so angry', 生氣 shēng qì 'to be angry'. Also means air or gas, as in 空氣 kōng qì 'air' and 天氣 tiān qì 'weather'.
MOE lists both fāng xiàng and a lighter fāng xiang; Taiwan speech keeps the full tone.
Physical injury, but also hurt feelings: 我很受傷 wǒ hěn shòu shāng 'I'm hurt'.
Also a verb: 公司規定 gōng sī guī dìng… 'company rules say…'.

hint: as a rule, most of the time

example.english: I usually get up at seven.

note: Literally 'add fuel'. Shouted to encourage or cheer someone on. Also literal: 去加油 qù jiā yóu 'go get gas'.

example.english: You've got an exam tomorrow. Good luck!

note: Common pairs: 犯錯 fàn cuò 'make a mistake', 犯法 fàn fǎ 'break the law', 犯人 fàn rén 'prisoner'.

example.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu huì fàncuò.

note: Used for things on the head, face or hands: 戴眼鏡 dài yǎn jìng 'wear glasses', 戴口罩 dài kǒu zhào 'wear a mask'. Clothes and shoes take 穿 chuān. Sounds the same as 帶 dài 'to bring'.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, dài màozi ba.
example.english: It's cold out, wear a hat.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn wǒ de jiārén.

note: Taiwan (MOE) says cōng míng with a full tone; the mainland says cōng ming.
車票 chē piào 'train/bus ticket', 電影票 diàn yǐng piào 'movie ticket', 投票 tóu piào 'to vote'. Counted with 張 zhāng. MOE's other reading piāo is literary and rare.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng piào.

note: The second syllable is dì (as in 目的地 mù dì dì 'destination'), not the particle de.

example.trad: 你來這裡的目的是什麼？
example.pinyin: Nǐ lái zhèlǐ de mùdì shì shénme?
example.english: What's your purpose in coming here?

note: Often 秒鐘 miǎo zhōng. Slang 秒殺 miǎo shā 'sold out in seconds'.
With a clause it usually means 'suspect that…' (我懷疑他在說謊 wǒ huái yí tā zài shuō huǎng); with a thing it can mean 'doubt' (懷疑自己 huái yí zì jǐ 'doubt yourself').
For a short person, use 矮 ǎi, not 低 dī. As a verb: 低頭 dī tóu 'lower one's head'.
Pattern 一旦 yī dàn…就 jiù… 'once X happens, then Y'. Spoken yí dàn (tone sandhi of 一 yī).

example.english: Once you start, you can't stop.

example.pinyin: Nǐ yào bù yào hē kāfēi?

note: Emphatic 'how' in exclamations, a bit literary; casual speech uses 多 duō or 好 hǎo: 好漂亮 hǎo piào liang! MOE gives duó me, but most Taiwanese say duō me.

example.pinyin: Nǐ bù zhīdào wǒ duōme xiǎng nǐ.
example.english: You don't know how much I miss you.

note: Also an adjective ('difficult'), but 難 nán is the everyday 'hard'. MOE gives kùn nan; many Taiwanese say kùn nán.

example.pinyin: Yǒu kùnnan jiù gēn wǒ shuō.
example.english: If you run into trouble, tell me.

note: Goes before an adjective or verb: 越來越冷 yuè lái yuè lěng 'colder and colder'. Not in MOE as a word; each syllable keeps its full tone.

example.english: I like Taiwan more and more.

note: Sounds written or poetic. In speech people say 漂亮 piào liang or 好美 hǎo měi.

example.pinyin: Táiwān shì ge měilì de dìfāng.
Néng rènshi nǐ, wǒ hěn xìngyùn.

note: In Taiwan the normal word for a girl or woman of any age up to middle age, not just a schoolgirl; its pair is 男生 nán shēng 'guy'. Mainland 姑娘 gū niang is rarely heard.
Taiwan word; the mainland says 網絡 wǎng luò. 上網 shàng wǎng 'to go online'.

example.english: The internet at home is so slow.

hint: the whole leg, not the foot
note: 腳 jiǎo is 'foot', though Taiwanese often say 腳 jiǎo for the leg too. Counted with 條 tiáo or 雙 shuāng.

example.pinyin: Pǎowán bù, wǒ de tuǐ hǎo tòng.
example.english: My legs really hurt after running.

note: The second syllable is chù 'place'; in 處理 chǔ lǐ 'to handle' it is chǔ.

example.english: I was just looking everywhere for you!

note: Experience as know-how. For events you lived through, 經歷 jīng lì is used.

example.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu kāichē de jīngyàn ma?
example.english: Do you have any driving experience?

note: Also used before a verb to mean 'officially': 正式開始 zhèng shì kāi shǐ 'officially start'.
A slightly more formal 'enough'. In everyday speech plain 夠 gòu is more common: 錢不夠 qián bù gòu 'not enough money'.
To have surgery is 動手術 dòng shǒu shù, or in casual Taiwan speech 開刀 kāi dāo.

example.trad: 我爸爸下個月要動手術。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bàba xià ge yuè yào dòng shǒushù.
example.english: My dad is having surgery next month.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì sòng nǐ de lǐwù.
example.english: This is a gift for you.

note: Also means going after someone romantically: 追女生 zhuī nǚ shēng 'to court a girl'. Also used for following a TV series: 追劇 zhuī jù. The rare literary reading duī means 'to carve'.

example.pinyin: Tā zhuī le tā liǎng nián.
example.english: He pursued her for two years.

note: Taiwan (MOE) says tóu fǎ with a full third tone. Mainland speech says tóu fa.
Counts large, fixed things: 一座山 yī zuò shān, 一座橋 yī zuò qiáo, 一座廟 yī zuò miào. Buildings are usually counted with 棟 dòng in Taiwan. 'Seat' is 座位 zuò wèi.

hint: can follow a time word, like tomorrow
note: Usually in the pattern 就要 jiù yào…了 le 'about to happen'. Unlike 快要 kuài yào, it can follow a time word: 明天就要走了 míng tiān jiù yào zǒu le 'leaving tomorrow already'. Can also mean 'just want': 我就要這個 wǒ jiù yào zhè ge.

example.english: The movie is about to start.

note: As a reply it means 'whatever, anything is fine'. Said of a person it means careless or sloppy: 他做事很隨便 tā zuò shì hěn suí biàn.

不 bù + 會 huì: 'will not' (他不會來 tā bù huì lái 'he won't come') or 'can't, never learned' (我不會游泳 wǒ bù huì yóu yǒng). In Taiwan it is also the usual reply to 謝謝 xiè xie: 'no problem'. 不 bù is spoken bú before huì.

example.pinyin: Fàngxīn, tā bù huì shēngqì de.
example.english: Don't worry, he won't be angry.

note: A body movement or gesture. In Taiwan 動作快一點 dòng zuò kuài yī diǎn is a common way to say 'hurry up'.

example.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ huīfù de hěn hǎo.

note: A general, slightly formal word. In casual speech people often say 吃的 chī de or 東西 dōng xi.
Counted with 隻 zhī: 一隻貓 yī zhī māo.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng zhī māo.
example.english: We have two cats at home.

gloss: quite a lot; quite a few
note: An understated 'a lot', literally 'not few'. 不 bù keeps its 4th tone here because 少 shǎo is a 3rd tone.

example.english: There are quite a few people today.

note: Most often an exclamation when something goes wrong. It can also describe a situation: 很糟糕 hěn zāo gāo 'really bad'.

example.pinyin: Zāogāo, wǒ wàng le dài yàoshi!
example.english: Oh no, I forgot my keys!

note: 恐怖片 kǒng bù piàn is a horror movie. Taiwanese also use it loosely for anything awful: 好恐怖 hǎo kǒng bù 'that's horrible'. Close to 可怕 kě pà.

example.english: I'm too scared to watch horror movies.

note: Before a verb it means 'for nothing': 白跑一趟 bái pǎo yī tàng 'a wasted trip'. The color is usually said 白色 bái sè. MOE also lists a literary reading bó.

example.pinyin: Tā de tóufǎ dōu bái le.
example.english: His hair has all turned white.

note: A slightly more formal 更 gèng. In everyday speech plain 更 gèng is more common.

example.pinyin: Tā biàn de gèngjiā nǔlì le.
